name: Credential
examples: OIDC access or refresh tokens provider sessions AWS keys Kubernetes tokens kubeconfigs private keys passwords secret values and database credentials
at_rest: Raw values exist only in process memory or an external secret manager; Veer persists opaque references versions and non-secret destination metadata; every unavoidable store is encrypted
in_transit: TLS with verified destination directly from broker to the single scoped recipient; never a queue body plan resource status or telemetry field
access: Credential broker and one bound adapter operation only; no human readback API; provider-side break-glass remains external and audited
logging: Forbidden in resources plans state queues fixtures logs traces metrics errors cost reports and support output; secret canaries must prove absence
retention: Raw session material only until operation completion expiry revocation cancellation or lost ownership; references follow ProviderConnection lifetime and independent rotation
disposal: Discard bounded buffers and caches on every terminal path; revoke or rotate provider identity; delete references through audited lifecycle without copying values into tombstones

name: Audit
examples: Actor and authentication method action target policy decision request operation provider attempt outcome timestamp source integrity and elevation reason
at_rest: Future production storage must use encrypted append-only relational records with independently protected integrity anchors and immutable encrypted object archive; the reference contract persists nothing and prohibits secret values and raw request or response bodies
in_transit: Future query export replication and recovery transport requires TLS; the reference export format binds verifiable sequence integrity manifest and scope but carries no credential material
access: Future Workspace-scoped authorized readers; separate security or platform operator access requires strong authenticated scoped audited elevation; future runtime authority may append but must not mutate or delete
logging: Security events belong here rather than only in platform logs; ordinary logs may carry an opaque event or operation ID but not duplicate sensitive audit payload
retention: The reference evaluator fixes 90 days online and 365 days archive; future production must make those intervals effective, while shorter retention requires reviewed security decision and longer retention requires security privacy storage and cost review
disposal: Expire only through reviewed lifecycle after retention and legal or incident holds; reference chain verification detects gaps inside a presented range while deployed tail-deletion detection requires independently trusted terminal checkpoints

name: Personal
examples: OIDC issuer subject email or group claims workload subject source network identifiers actor attributes and other data linkable to a person
at_rest: Minimize to stable opaque principal and required policy attributes; encrypt every persisted enclosing record; raw tokens are credential class and never stored
in_transit: TLS only to authentication policy scoped audit and authorized administration; never provider requests queue payloads or metric dimensions unless a reviewed requirement adds it
access: The subject and workspace-authorized identity administrators see the minimum needed; security access follows scoped audited elevation; providers receive no personal claim by default
logging: Never log raw tokens; omit email group source address and actor identifiers from metric labels; use opaque bounded correlation and redact errors or support output
retention: No independent convenience copy; follows the enclosing membership resource audit log or trace boundary; audit portions use 90 and 365 days while platform logs use 14 or 30 days and traces 7 days
disposal: Expire with the enclosing record and backup lifecycle; identity deletion or correction follows reviewed policy without rewriting immutable audit; minimize future exposure with pseudonymous identifiers

name: Configuration
examples: Desired resource specifications policies manifests provider secret references non-secret endpoints plans approvals quota cost and capability inputs
at_rest: Encrypted authoritative store with stable workspace ownership generation integrity anchor and immutable plan or decision; secret references are allowed but referenced values are credential class
in_transit: TLS through API store and adapter boundaries; queue carries stable IDs generation and digest rather than full configuration; provider receives only the required validated subset
access: Workspace and environment roles by action; worker receives current scoped snapshot; provider adapter receives only plan-required fields; platform access is separately audited
logging: No raw payload by default; validation may report bounded field paths and safe reasons; redact sensitive values and never emit connection strings endpoints containing credentials or arbitrary provider bodies
retention: Current state for resource lifetime plus 90-day tombstone; operations plans and policy decisions 90 days online and 365 days encrypted archive; backups follow 35-day primary and 7-day recovery windows
disposal: Tombstone then expire through lifecycle; remove provider-side resources only with ownership proof; backup copies age out by policy and deletion cannot erase required audit evidence

name: Operational
examples: Status conditions health errors provider error classes correlation IDs external IDs drift quota cost metrics logs traces queue depth and saturation
at_rest: Encrypted service stores selected by subtype with bounded payload bytes cardinality and dimensions; security events are promoted to audit instead of relying on logs
in_transit: TLS to authorized API clients operators and configured exporters; exporter failure cannot stop reconciliation and no secret or raw user payload is sent
access: Workspace-scoped status for users; bounded platform-wide health for operators; exporter and cost systems receive only allowlisted low-sensitivity fields
logging: This class supplies redacted logs traces and metrics; workspace resource request provider object and actor IDs are forbidden metric labels; errors use stable safe classes
retention: Platform logs 14 days small or 30 days target; traces 7 days; high-resolution metrics 15 days and SLO rollups 13 months; status and conditions follow owning resource; shorter subtype limits are preferred
disposal: Automatic TTL or resource lifecycle expiry; dropped telemetry is counted without retaining dropped content; no operational deletion may remove required audit or recovery evidence
